title: Normalized right-derived ringed-edge data and composite path maps
statement: Use the size convention [def-weil-size-convention], the corner and edge presentations [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-square-presentation], and the unbounded localizations $Q$ and $Q_h$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For an edge $e:A\to B$ in inverse-image direction, write $P_e,F_e,L_e,R_e$ for its ordinary pullback, ordinary direct image, derived pullback and specified derived right adjoint. The normalized right-derived datum consists of additivity of $F_e$, a natural transformation $\eta_e:Q\circ C(F_e)\to R_e\circ Q$ making $R_e$ the total right derived functor of $C(F_e)$ at quasi-isomorphisms, and the following normalization. For all complexes $M$ on $A$, $I$ on $B$, and chain maps $a:C(P_e)M\to I$, the derived adjunction sends $Q(a)\circ\alpha_{e,M}$ to $\eta_{e,I}\circ Q(\operatorname{adj}_e(a))$, where $\alpha_e:L_eQ\to QC(P_e)$ is induced by the edge's left-derived comparison and $\operatorname{adj}_e$ is its ordinary module adjunction on complexes. For composable edges $f:X\to W$, $g:Y\to X$, define the right path unit for $F_gF_f$ to be $R_g(\eta_f)\circ\eta_g C(F_f)$, with the functor-composition identifications. Define the left path counit for $L_fL_g$ to be the composite of the two left-derived counits, from $L_fL_gQ_h$ to $Q_hK(P_fP_g)$, with the functor-composition identifications. Finally, given tensor models $a_W,a_X,a_Y$, define the path tensor map at $K,H\in D(Y)$ by applying $L_f$ to the canonical tensor-pullback map for $g$ and then the canonical tensor-pullback map for $f$ at $(L_gK,L_gH)$. These are data and composites, with no extra coherence assertion or hypothesis on boundedness.
